Bunk based on?

The world is awash in mineral wealth - when there are shortages it occurs simply because people are not digging it up at that particular time. The markets ebb and flow, and prices dictate the mining activity - but there are large investments and large lead times associated with starting and operating mines - and market prices are also affected by finance trading, above and beyond normal supply and demand, which further warps the cycle.

Another factor is that a large percentage of the rarer minerals come as byproducts of mining operations aimed at other markets. For example, at least half of the annual global production of silver comes as a byproduct of mining other minerals. Take the nickel mine in Sudbury Ontario - the main resource mined is nickel, but they also produce gold and silver and a few other metals there. It is not an issue of the presence of the other metals - it is always a question of if there is enough volume, at today's (and tomorrow's) prices to warrant investing in a separation process.

Wherever you find valuable metals, you also tend to find the other valuable metals as well - the main difference in whether you have a gold mine or a silver mine is often which metal is there in the greatest percentage quantity. Valuable materials are found almost universally everywhere - the issue then is is it worthwhile to make the necessary long term investments needed to bother to dig it up.
